sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xv+181 pp.
sources.note: Intro sec. 7 (pp. vii-viii): 'The transcription of the word list is rendered in a semiphonemic form, i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; fluctuation table gives Urigina d ~ r. List B16 Urigina entries carry no stress marks (page image printed p. 16: 'eye' ʌŋki-, 'mouth' sɛmbɛ-). No statement on stress or accent anywhere; note 3 p. 172 'the Dumpu-Watiwa language is tonal' concerns B5, not Urigina.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.21.2 (pp. 36-37): Urigina 16/Ur, 1,790 speakers, 'previously unrecorded'. Sec. 2.21.23 Typological features of the Usur Group (pp. 37-38, pdf p. 45): voiced stops in Urigina 'appear to be all prenasalized', velar nasal only in those; 'words tend to end in a vowel'; nothing on stress/accent/tone. Sec. 2.21.5 Madang Phylum typology (pp. 41-42): phoneme-inventory remarks only. The 'none of the languages appears to be tonal' lines (2.22.8, 2.23.x) concern the Adelbert Range and Ramu phyla, not Urigina.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University. x+335 pp. hdl:1885/130077
sources.note: Sec. 1.3, printed p. 13 (pdf p. 22): broad phonetic transcription after Pike 1947; 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'
